131	This Executive Summary presents the findings of a Phase I Environmental Site Assessment (\"Phase I ESA\") conducted in accordance with ASTM E1527-21, *Standard Practice for Environmental Site Assessments: Phase I Environmental Site Assessment Process*, for the property known as Meridian Corporate Center, located at 11600, 11620, and 11640 Corporate Park Drive, Reston, Virginia 20191 (the \"Subject Property\" or \"Property\").
132	
133	The assessment was commissioned by Calverley Capital Partners LLC (the \"Client\") in connection with a proposed acquisition of the Property from Meridian Office Holdings LP (the \"Seller\"). The purpose of this Phase I ESA is to identify Recognized Environmental Conditions (\"RECs\"), Controlled Recognized Environmental Conditions (\"CRECs\"), and Historical Recognized Environmental Conditions (\"HRECs\") in connection with the Subject Property, as those terms are defined under ASTM E1527-21.
134	
135	This assessment is intended to satisfy the \"All Appropriate Inquiries\" (\"AAI\") standard codified at 40 CFR Part 312, promulgated by the United States Environmental Protection Agency pursuant to the Small Business Liability Relief and Brownfields Revitalization Act of 2002. Compliance with the AAI standard qualifies the Client for certain liability protections available under the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (\"CERCLA\"), 42 U.S.C. §§ 9601 *et seq.*, including the \"innocent landowner,\" \"contiguous property owner,\" and \"bona fide prospective purchaser\" defenses.
136	
137	The scope of this Phase I ESA includes: (i) a review of federal, state, tribal, and local regulatory agency records and databases; (ii) a review of historical sources, including aerial photographs, Sanborn Fire Insurance Maps, topographic maps, building permits, land records, and city directories; (iii) a site reconnaissance of the Subject Property and visual observation of adjoining properties; (iv) interviews with knowledgeable parties regarding the environmental history and condition of the Subject Property; and (v) evaluation of the Subject Property and adjoining properties for evidence of potential environmental conditions.
138	
139	Site reconnaissance was conducted on July 29--30, 2024, by Dr. Karen M. Whitfield, P.G., Senior Environmental Scientist with Clearfield Environmental Consulting LLC. Interviews were conducted with Marcus Ellison, President of Meridian GP Inc. (the general partner of the Seller), and members of the on-site property management team retained by the Seller.
140	
141	This document is an Executive Summary. The full Phase I ESA report contains detailed findings, methodology descriptions, appendices, regulatory database search results, historical documentation, site photographs, and the complete limiting conditions and qualifications applicable to this assessment.
142	
143	**[Section 2: Property Description]{.underline}**
144	
145	**Property Name:** Meridian Corporate Center
146	
147	**Addresses:** 11600 Corporate Park Drive (Building A), 11620 Corporate Park Drive (Building B), and 11640 Corporate Park Drive (Building C), Reston, Virginia 20191, Fairfax County, Virginia
148	
149	**Tax Map Parcels:** 0264-01-0017A, 0264-01-0017B, and 0264-01-0017C (Fairfax County)
150	
151	**Total Acreage:** Approximately 22.8 acres
152	
153	**Improvements:** The Subject Property is improved with three Class A suburban office buildings constructed in 2013, totaling approximately 312,000 rentable square feet. Building A (11600 Corporate Park Drive) contains approximately 118,000 rentable square feet. Building B (11620 Corporate Park Drive) contains approximately 104,000 rentable square feet. Building C (11640 Corporate Park Drive) contains approximately 90,000 rentable square feet. The buildings are steel-frame, glass-curtain-wall construction, each ranging from four to five stories in height.
154	
155	**Structured Parking Garage:** The Subject Property includes a structured parking garage containing approximately 1,248 parking spaces, providing a parking ratio of approximately 4.0 spaces per 1,000 rentable square feet of office space.
156	
157	**Current Occupancy:** The Subject Property is approximately 82% occupied by 14 commercial tenants. Tenant uses consist primarily of professional office, professional services, technology, and government contractor operations. No industrial, manufacturing, laboratory, or chemical-intensive tenant uses were identified.
158	
159	**Site Topography:** The Subject Property exhibits generally flat to gently sloping terrain. Surface drainage is directed toward the southwest, consistent with the area\'s natural topographic gradient. The southwest portion of the site, in the vicinity of Building C, is at a slightly lower elevation than the northeast portion of the site where Building A is located. Elevation across the site ranges from approximately 340 feet above mean sea level (northeast) to approximately 325 feet above mean sea level (southwest).
160	
161	**Utilities:** The Subject Property is served by public water (Fairfax Water) and public sewer (Fairfax County Wastewater Management Program). No private water supply wells or on-site septic systems were identified during the assessment.
162	
163	**Prior Use of Subject Property:** Prior to 2011, the Subject Property consisted of undeveloped land zoned for planned development within the Reston community. Site grading and construction activities commenced in 2012, and building construction was substantially completed in 2013. Based on the historical sources reviewed, no prior commercial, industrial, agricultural, or other potentially contaminating use of the Subject Property was identified during any period of record.
164	
165	**Current Owner:** Meridian Office Holdings LP, a Virginia limited partnership formed on September 22, 2011. Meridian Office Holdings LP developed the Subject Property and has continuously held fee simple ownership of the Property since construction. The general partner of Meridian Office Holdings LP is Meridian GP Inc., a Virginia corporation.
166	
167	**[Section 3: Historical Use Review]{.underline}**
168	
169	**Methodology.** The historical use review was conducted in accordance with the requirements of ASTM E1527-21, Section 8.3. Historical sources reviewed include: Sanborn Fire Insurance Maps (where available for the Subject Property and surrounding area); historical aerial photographs dated 1957, 1971, 1983, 1994, 2002, 2010, 2015, and 2020; historical topographic maps from the United States Geological Survey (USGS) 7.5-minute quadrangle series; Fairfax County building permits and land records; and historical city directories for the Reston, Virginia area.
170	
171	**Subject Property History**
172	
173	Review of historical aerial photographs from 1957 through 2002 consistently depicts the Subject Property as undeveloped woodland and scrubland, with no structures, cleared areas, or evidence of any commercial, industrial, or agricultural use visible in any photograph during this period. No Sanborn Fire Insurance Maps were available for the Subject Property itself, as the Property was located outside of the historically mapped areas until the expansion of suburban development in western Fairfax County in recent decades.
174	
175	The 2010 aerial photograph shows active grading and site preparation on the Subject Property, consistent with the commencement of construction activities in 2012. The 2015 aerial photograph depicts the three office buildings and the structured parking garage, consistent with the 2013 construction completion date confirmed by Fairfax County certificate of occupancy records.
176	
177	No evidence of underground storage tanks (USTs), above-ground storage tanks (ASTs), dry cleaning operations, gasoline service stations, manufacturing facilities, chemical storage, landfilling, or other potentially contaminating uses on the Subject Property was identified through the historical record review.
178	
179	**Adjoining Properties --- Critical Finding**
180	
181	The parcel immediately to the southwest of the Subject Property (Fairfax County Tax Map Parcel 0264-01-0019, an approximately 3.2-acre parcel currently improved with a retail strip center constructed circa 2006) formerly housed a commercial dry cleaning facility.
182	
183	Sanborn Fire Insurance Maps (1988 edition) and historical city directories for the Reston, Virginia area confirm that a commercial dry cleaning business operating under the name \"Reston Village Cleaners\" occupied a freestanding commercial building at the approximate location of the current retail strip center from approximately 1985 to 2003. The dry cleaning operation utilized tetrachloroethylene (also known as perchloroethylene, or \"PCE\") as its primary dry cleaning solvent, as confirmed by Virginia Department of Environmental Quality (\"DEQ\") records and historical business permit filings with Fairfax County.
184	
185	The former dry cleaning building was demolished in approximately 2004--2005 in connection with redevelopment of the adjacent parcel. The existing retail strip center was constructed in 2006 by an unrelated developer.
186	
187	Virginia DEQ records indicate that a Voluntary Remediation Program (\"VRP\") case (VRP File No. VRP-00487) was opened for the adjacent parcel in 2004 in connection with the planned redevelopment. DEQ records indicate that soil sampling conducted during the VRP investigation process in 2004 identified PCE concentrations in soil at levels exceeding the Virginia Voluntary Remediation Program Tier II screening levels applicable at that time. Limited soil remediation, consisting of excavation and off-site disposal of approximately 200 cubic yards of PCE-impacted soil, was conducted in 2005. The Virginia DEQ issued a Certificate of Satisfactory Completion of Remediation in March 2006 for the adjacent parcel only.
188	
189	However, the DEQ VRP file indicates that groundwater sampling conducted during the 2004--2005 investigation detected PCE in groundwater at concentrations up to 87 micrograms per liter (µg/L) in a monitoring well located on the southern boundary of the adjacent parcel. The applicable Virginia Groundwater Quality Standard for PCE is 5 µg/L, meaning the detected concentration exceeded the applicable standard by a factor of approximately 17.4. The VRP closure letter issued by DEQ in March 2006 included the following notation: \"groundwater impacts associated with the former dry cleaning operation may extend beyond the boundaries of the Property\" and that \"further investigation of potential off-site migration may be warranted.\" The closure letter did not require further action by the VRP applicant with respect to potential off-site contamination.
190	
191	Regional groundwater flow direction in the vicinity of the Subject Property, based on USGS hydrogeologic data and Fairfax County hydrogeologic mapping, is generally from the northeast to the southwest. However, localized groundwater flow patterns in the immediate area may be influenced by the structured parking garage foundation, building foundations, and stormwater management features constructed on the Subject Property, potentially creating a more complex groundwater flow regime than the regional pattern would suggest. The Subject Property --- specifically the southwest corner of the site where Building C (11640 Corporate Park Drive) is located --- is cross-gradient to slightly downgradient from the location of the former dry cleaning facility on the adjacent parcel.
192	
193	**Other Adjoining Properties**
194	
195	No other adjoining properties were identified with environmental conditions of concern. Properties to the north and east of the Subject Property consist of commercial office developments of similar vintage to the Subject Property. The property to the west of the Subject Property is a Fairfax County parkland parcel with no identified prior commercial, industrial, or other potentially contaminating use.
196	
197	**[Section 4: Regulatory Database Review]{.underline}**
198	
199	**Methodology.** A standard ASTM E1527-21 environmental regulatory database search was conducted by Environmental DataLink Services Inc. on July 15, 2024. The database search covered applicable federal, state, tribal, and local regulatory databases within the search radii specified by ASTM E1527-21, including but not limited to the EPA National Priorities List (NPL), CERCLIS/SEMS, RCRA CORRACTS, RCRA TSD, RCRA SQG/LQG, ERNS, Virginia DEQ Solid Waste facilities, Virginia DEQ Underground Storage Tank (UST) database, Virginia DEQ Voluntary Remediation Program (VRP) database, Virginia DEQ Petroleum Release database, and Fairfax County environmental records.
200	
201	**Subject Property.** The Subject Property (Tax Map Parcels 0264-01-0017A, 0264-01-0017B, and 0264-01-0017C) is not listed in any federal, state, or local environmental regulatory database searched as part of this assessment. No enforcement actions, violations, spills, releases, or remediation activities associated with the Subject Property were identified.
202	
203	**Adjacent Parcel (Tax Map Parcel 0264-01-0019).** The parcel immediately to the southwest of the Subject Property is listed in the following databases:
204	
205	> • **Virginia DEQ Voluntary Remediation Program (VRP) Database** --- VRP File No. VRP-00487. Case status: Closed. Certificate of Satisfactory Completion of Remediation issued March 2006. The VRP closure addressed the adjacent parcel only and, as discussed in Section 3 above, included an explicit notation that groundwater impacts may extend beyond the boundaries of that parcel.
206	>
207	> • **Virginia DEQ Underground Storage Tank (UST) Database** --- One 500-gallon heating oil underground storage tank was removed from the former dry cleaning facility site in 2004 during redevelopment activities. The UST closure letter issued by DEQ indicated that no petroleum release was detected in connection with the tank removal, and no further action was required with respect to the UST.
208	
209	**Other Nearby Facilities.** One facility located at 11580 Corporate Park Drive, approximately 0.3 miles to the northeast of the Subject Property, is listed as a RCRA Small Quantity Generator (SQG). The facility is identified as a commercial printing operation. No violations, releases, or corrective action requirements are associated with this listing. This facility is outside the ASTM-specified search radius for concern relative to the Subject Property and is not considered to represent a potential environmental concern.
210	
211	No other facilities within applicable ASTM search radii were identified as posing a potential environmental concern to the Subject Property.
212	
213	The regulatory database findings corroborate the historical use review findings discussed in Section 3 and confirm that while the adjacent parcel was remediated and closed under the VRP program, the closure was explicitly limited to the adjacent parcel and did not address the potential for off-site groundwater migration of PCE toward the Subject Property.
214	
215	**[Section 5: Site Reconnaissance Observations]{.underline}**
216	
217	**Date of Site Visit:** July 29--30, 2024
218	
219	**Conducted by:** Dr. Karen M. Whitfield, P.G., Senior Environmental Scientist, Clearfield Environmental Consulting LLC
220	
221	**General Observations.** The three office buildings and the structured parking garage are in good overall condition, consistent with their 2013 construction date. Building systems, including heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC), plumbing, fire suppression, and electrical systems, appeared to be well-maintained based on visual observation and review of available maintenance records. No evidence of hazardous materials storage, underground storage tanks, above-ground storage tanks, drums, or chemical containers (other than de minimis quantities of building maintenance supplies as noted in Section 6.4) was observed on the Subject Property.
222	
223	**Specific Observations. Asbestos-Containing Materials (ACM).** Given the 2013 construction date, the buildings are unlikely to contain asbestos-containing materials. No suspect ACM was observed during the site reconnaissance. Review of the building\'s Operations and Maintenance (O&M) plan and original construction specifications, provided by the property management team, confirms that no ACM was specified or used in the construction of the buildings.
224	
225	**Lead-Based Paint (LBP).** Not applicable. All buildings on the Subject Property post-date the Consumer Product Safety Commission\'s 1978 ban on lead-based paint in residential and commercial applications.
226	
227	**Polychlorinated Biphenyls (PCBs).** No PCB-containing transformers, capacitors, or other electrical equipment was identified on the Subject Property. Pad-mounted electrical transformers serving the buildings are labeled as containing non-PCB dielectric fluid.
228	
229	**Mold and Indoor Air Quality.** No evidence of active water intrusion, water damage, or visible mold growth was observed in any of the buildings during the site visit. A comprehensive indoor air quality assessment or mold investigation was not within the scope of this Phase I ESA.
230	
231	**Stormwater Management.** The Subject Property has an on-site stormwater management system, including two stormwater retention ponds located along the southern and western boundaries of the site. The ponds appeared to be functioning properly at the time of the site visit. Maintenance records and inspection reports for the stormwater system were provided by the property management team and appear consistent with Fairfax County maintenance requirements.
232	
233	**Southwest Corner of Building C.** The area of the Subject Property closest to the adjacent former dry cleaning parcel (Tax Map Parcel 0264-01-0019) was visually inspected during the site reconnaissance. No surficial staining, stressed or discolored vegetation, unusual odors, or other visual indicators of contamination were observed in this area. However, visual inspection alone is not sufficient to determine the presence or absence of subsurface contamination from migrating chlorinated solvents such as PCE, which may be present in groundwater at depths below the surface without producing visible surface indicators.
234	
235	**Interviews.** Marcus Ellison, President of Meridian GP Inc. (the general partner of the Seller), stated during an interview conducted on July 29, 2024, that he was not aware of any environmental contamination affecting the Subject Property. Mr. Ellison confirmed that he was aware of the former dry cleaning operation on the adjacent parcel and the VRP remediation conducted in 2004--2006 but stated that he had no knowledge of off-site contamination migration onto the Subject Property. Mr. Ellison further stated that no environmental testing of soil or groundwater has been conducted on the Subject Property.
236	
237	On-site property management staff, interviewed on July 30, 2024, reported no complaints from tenants in Building C or any other building regarding chemical odors, health concerns, or other issues potentially related to solvent contamination or vapor intrusion. No indoor air quality testing has been conducted in any building on the Subject Property.
238	
239	**[Section 6: Findings and Opinions]{.underline}**
240	
241	**6.1 Recognized Environmental Conditions (RECs)**
242	
243	**One (1) Recognized Environmental Condition was identified in connection with the Subject Property:**
244	
245	**REC-1: Potential Tetrachloroethylene (PCE) Groundwater Migration from Adjacent Former Dry Cleaning Facility**
246	
247	A former commercial dry cleaning facility (\"Reston Village Cleaners\") operated on the parcel immediately to the southwest of the Subject Property (Fairfax County Tax Map Parcel 0264-01-0019) from approximately 1985 to 2003. Tetrachloroethylene (also known as perchloroethylene, or \"PCE\") was used as the primary dry cleaning solvent at the facility. Virginia DEQ Voluntary Remediation Program records (VRP File No. VRP-00487) document both soil and groundwater contamination at the former dry cleaning site. PCE was detected in groundwater at concentrations up to 87 µg/L in a monitoring well located on the southern boundary of the adjacent parcel --- a concentration significantly exceeding the Virginia Groundwater Quality Standard for PCE of 5 µg/L (an exceedance factor of approximately 17.4 times the standard).
248	
249	The VRP closure issued by Virginia DEQ in March 2006 addressed the adjacent parcel only. The closure letter explicitly noted that \"groundwater impacts associated with the former dry cleaning operation may extend beyond the boundaries of the Property\" and that \"further investigation of potential off-site migration may be warranted.\" No investigation of potential off-site migration toward the Subject Property has been conducted.
250	
251	Regional groundwater flow direction is generally from the northeast to the southwest. The Subject Property, specifically the southwest corner of the site where Building C (11640 Corporate Park Drive) is situated, is cross-gradient to slightly downgradient of the former dry cleaning facility location. This hydrogeologic positioning means that PCE-impacted groundwater could be migrating from the adjacent parcel toward and potentially beneath the Subject Property, particularly in the vicinity of Building C.
252	
253	PCE is a dense non-aqueous phase liquid (DNAPL) that, once released into the subsurface environment, can migrate vertically through soil and horizontally through groundwater over significant distances. The fractured rock and alluvial aquifer systems characteristic of the Reston, Virginia area are particularly susceptible to DNAPL migration through preferential flow pathways in bedrock fractures.
254	
255	**Based on the foregoing, Clearfield considers the potential migration of PCE-impacted groundwater from the adjacent parcel onto the Subject Property to constitute a Recognized Environmental Condition as defined by ASTM E1527-21.**
256	
257	PCE is a chlorinated volatile organic compound classified by the United States Environmental Protection Agency as a likely human carcinogen. PCE contamination plumes originating from dry cleaning facilities are well-documented in the environmental remediation literature to require extensive and costly investigation and remediation programs. Depending on the nature, extent, and severity of contamination, remediation approaches may include groundwater extraction and treatment (pump-and-treat systems), soil vapor extraction (SVE), in-situ chemical oxidation (ISCO), enhanced reductive dechlorination (ERD), or long-term monitored natural attenuation (MNA), or some combination of these technologies. Remediation costs for PCE dry cleaner contamination vary widely but commonly range from several hundred thousand dollars to in excess of \$5,000,000, and in cases involving extensive groundwater plumes, DNAPL presence at depth, or vapor intrusion concerns requiring building mitigation, costs can exceed \$10,000,000.
258	
259	**6.2 Controlled Recognized Environmental Conditions (CRECs)**
260	
261	No Controlled Recognized Environmental Conditions were identified in connection with the Subject Property.
262	
263	**6.3 Historical Recognized Environmental Conditions (HRECs)**
264	
265	No Historical Recognized Environmental Conditions were identified in connection with the Subject Property.
266	
267	**6.4 De Minimis Conditions**
268	
269	**DMC-1:** Minor quantities of typical commercial building maintenance chemicals --- including general-purpose cleaning supplies, touch-up paint, and mechanical lubricants --- were observed in properly labeled containers in designated maintenance storage areas within each building. These materials are present in quantities and conditions consistent with normal commercial building operations and are not considered to represent environmental concerns.
270	
271	**6.5 Business Environmental Risks --- Not Within ASTM E1527-21 Scope but Noted for Informational Purposes**
272	
273	**Vapor Intrusion Potential.** If PCE-impacted groundwater has migrated from the adjacent former dry cleaning parcel beneath the Subject Property, there is a potential risk of vapor intrusion into Building C and potentially into other buildings on the Subject Property. Vapor intrusion is a process by which volatile organic compounds (VOCs) present in contaminated soil or groundwater volatilize and migrate upward through the unsaturated soil zone and building foundations into indoor air, potentially resulting in exposure to building occupants at concentrations of health concern. While no tenant complaints or chemical odors were noted during the site visit, and no visual indicators of vapor intrusion were observed, vapor intrusion assessment is not within the standard scope of a Phase I ESA and would require a Phase II investigation incorporating sub-slab soil gas sampling and/or indoor air sampling to evaluate.
274	
275	This observation is provided for informational purposes as a Business Environmental Risk and is outside the scope of ASTM E1527-21 but is considered relevant to the Client\'s transaction decision-making and risk assessment.
276	
277	**[Section 7: Recommendations]{.underline}**
278	
279	**Primary Recommendation --- Phase II Environmental Site Assessment**
280	
281	Clearfield recommends that a Phase II Environmental Site Assessment be conducted prior to or as a condition of the proposed acquisition to evaluate the potential migration of PCE-impacted groundwater from the adjacent former dry cleaning facility (Tax Map Parcel 0264-01-0019) onto the Subject Property. The Phase II investigation should include, at a minimum, the following scope:
282	
283	> 1\. **Installation of Groundwater Monitoring Wells.** A minimum of three groundwater monitoring wells should be installed along the southwestern boundary of the Subject Property, positioned between the former dry cleaning facility site and Building C, to delineate the lateral and vertical extent of any PCE groundwater contamination plume that may have migrated onto the Subject Property.
284	>
285	> 2\. **Groundwater Sampling and Laboratory Analysis.** Groundwater samples should be collected from the newly installed monitoring wells and analyzed for volatile organic compounds (VOCs) by EPA Method 8260, with particular attention to PCE and its common degradation products, including trichloroethylene (TCE), cis-1,2-dichloroethylene (cis-1,2-DCE), and vinyl chloride.
286	>
287	> 3\. **Sub-Slab Soil Gas Sampling.** Sub-slab soil gas sampling should be conducted beneath the ground-floor slab of the southwest corner of Building C (11640 Corporate Park Drive) to evaluate the potential for vapor intrusion of PCE and related VOCs into the building interior.
288	>
289	> 4\. **Indoor Air Sampling.** Indoor air sampling should be conducted in tenant spaces on the ground floor of Building C as warranted by the results of the sub-slab soil gas sampling program.
290	
291	The Phase II investigation should be designed and executed to determine whether contamination from the adjacent former dry cleaning site has migrated onto the Subject Property and, if contamination is present, to characterize the nature and extent of such contamination with sufficient detail to support estimation of potential remediation costs and assessment of the Client\'s liability exposure.
292	
293	**Estimated Phase II Cost.** Clearfield estimates the cost of the recommended Phase II investigation at approximately \$45,000 to \$65,000, depending on encountered subsurface conditions, the number of monitoring wells ultimately required, drilling conditions, and the scope of analytical testing indicated by initial results.
294	
295	**Timing.** Clearfield recommends that the Phase II investigation be initiated promptly given the Client\'s reported due diligence timeline. Clearfield can mobilize field work within approximately 10 to 14 business days of written authorization to proceed and anticipates providing preliminary analytical results within approximately four to six weeks following completion of field activities.
296	
297	**Additional Recommendation --- Virginia DEQ Coordination**
298	
299	Clearfield recommends that a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request be submitted to the Virginia Department of Environmental Quality for the complete VRP case file (VRP File No. VRP-00487) associated with the adjacent parcel (Tax Map Parcel 0264-01-0019). The complete file may contain additional sampling data, remedial action reports, monitoring well logs, contaminant fate-and-transport modeling, and the Certificate of Satisfactory Completion of Remediation with any associated conditions, restrictions, or institutional controls. Clearfield has reviewed summary records available through the DEQ online database system, but the complete case file may provide additional detail regarding the documented extent and migration direction of the PCE groundwater plume.
300	
301	**Additional Recommendation --- Review of Transaction Environmental Protections**
302	
303	Given the identified Recognized Environmental Condition, Clearfield recommends that the Client and its legal counsel carefully review any environmental indemnification provisions, environmental insurance policies, escrow arrangements, or other financial protections available to the Client in connection with the proposed acquisition transaction. The potential costs of investigation and remediation of a PCE groundwater plume, if present beneath the Subject Property, could be significant, and the Client should ensure that adequate financial protections are in place to address potential environmental liabilities associated with this condition.
304	
305	**[Section 8: Limiting Conditions and Qualifications]{.underline}**
306	
307	This Executive Summary is subject to the complete limiting conditions and qualifications set forth in Section 1.7 of the full Phase I ESA report (Report No. CEC-2024-0812-MCC). The following principal limiting conditions apply:
308	
309	> 1\. This assessment was performed in accordance with the scope and limitations of ASTM E1527-21. A Phase I Environmental Site Assessment is not designed to identify all environmental conditions that may exist at a property, but only those Recognized Environmental Conditions, Controlled Recognized Environmental Conditions, and Historical Recognized Environmental Conditions that are identifiable through the assessment methodology defined by the ASTM standard.
310	>
311	> 2\. No sampling, testing, or laboratory analysis of soil, groundwater, surface water, air, building materials, or other environmental media was conducted as part of this Phase I ESA. The findings and opinions expressed herein are based solely on records review, historical research, site reconnaissance, and interviews conducted in accordance with ASTM E1527-21.
312	>
313	> 3\. The findings and opinions expressed herein are based on information available to Clearfield Environmental Consulting LLC as of the date of this report. Environmental conditions at the Subject Property or adjoining properties may change over time, and Clearfield assumes no obligation to update this report based on conditions arising after the date of the assessment.
314	>
315	> 4\. This report was prepared for the exclusive use of Calverley Capital Partners LLC and its authorized agents, consultants, and lenders in connection with the proposed acquisition of the Subject Property. No other party may rely upon this report without the prior written consent of Clearfield Environmental Consulting LLC.
316	>
317	> 5\. Clearfield\'s liability in connection with this report is limited to the professional fee paid for this assessment, except as may otherwise be agreed in writing between Clearfield and the Client.
318	
319	**Reliance Authorization.** In addition to the Client, this report may be relied upon by the following parties, subject to the limiting conditions stated herein and in the full Phase I ESA report:
320	
321	> • Pinnacle National Bank, as prospective lender in connection with the proposed acquisition
322	>
323	> • Hargrave, Mitchell & Stone LLP, as legal counsel to the Client
324	>

328

I have performed this assessment in conformance with the standards and practices set forth in ASTM E1527-21.

**[PURCHASE AND SALE AGREEMENT]{.underline}**

This Purchase and Sale Agreement (this \"Agreement\") is made and entered into as of October 7, 2024 (the \"Effective Date\"), by and between **MERIDIAN OFFICE HOLDINGS LP**, a Virginia limited partnership (\"Seller\"), and **BRIDGEWATER CAPITAL PARTNERS LLC**, a Delaware limited liability company (\"Buyer\").

S=/home/user/Lawless_Research_Lab/harvey_lab/sbx.sh; R=/home/user/Lawless_Research_Lab/harvey_lab/vendor/harvey-labs/results/real-estate/extract-psa-key-terms/scenario-01/claude-code-session/20261016-030527; $S $R 'cat > /workspace/build/p2.py <<"EOF"
from h import *
H("Part III — Term Sheet by Topic", 1)
P("A “→ Flag” cross-reference in a row points to the related item in Part IV.", italic=True)

H("1. Parties and Transaction Participants", 2)
TERMS([
 ["Seller", "Preamble; §7.1(a)", "Meridian Office Holdings LP, a Virginia limited partnership formed September 22, 2011. Sole general partner: Meridian GP Inc. (Virginia corporation). Authorized signatory: Marcus Ellison, President of Meridian GP Inc. Seller’s notice address: 11700 Plaza America Drive, Suite 300, Reston, VA 20190."],
 ["Buyer (as named in PSA)", "Preamble; §7.5(a); signature page", "**Bridgewater Capital Partners LLC**, a Delaware limited liability company formed March 14, 2019. It is to be qualified to do business in Virginia before Closing. Signed by David Kowalski and Priya Venkataraman, each as Managing Member. → Flag 1"],
 ["Buyer notice party", "§15.2", "**Calverley Capital Partners LLC**, 2200 Pennsylvania Ave NW, Suite 800, Washington, DC 20037, Attn: Rebecca Thornton, GC (rthornton@bridgewatercap.com). Copy to Hargrave, Mitchell & Stone LLP, 1900 K Street NW, Suite 1200, Washington, DC 20006, Attn: Jonathan Hargrave (jhargrave@hmstone.com). → Flags 1, 27"],
 ["Seller’s counsel", "§15.2; Ex. C", "Ferndale & Aldrich LLP, 8300 Greensboro Drive, Suite 750, McLean, VA 22102, Attn: Sandra Aldrich, Esq. (listed e-mail: saldrich@fenwickaldrich.com). The firm prepared the deed. → Flag 27"],
 ["Escrow Agent / Title Company", "§1.1; §15.2; signature page", "Commonwealth Title & Escrow LLC (Virginia LLC), 1801 Robert Fulcroft Drive, Suite 200, Reston, VA 20191; Escrow Officer Jennifer Walsh (jwalsh@commonwealthtitle.com). Joins the PSA solely to acknowledge its Article III obligations. It is an intended third-party beneficiary of Article III (§15.10)."],
 ["Buyer’s lender", "§9.4; §10.2(a); Ex. E", "Pinnacle National Bank (or an affiliate). First mortgage loan of up to $57,037,500 (65% LTV). Loan officer: Thomas Brannigan (per instruction email)."],
 ["Brokers", "§15.1", "Seller’s broker: Greystone Realty Advisors LLC. Buyer’s broker: Keystone Commercial Partners LLC."],
 ["Seller knowledge party", "§7.1 (final para.)", "Actual knowledge of Marcus Ellison, without independent investigation, but with a duty to inquire of Seller’s on-site property manager. → Flag 4"],
])

H("2. Property Description", 2)
TERMS([
 ["Property", "§1.1 “Property”; §2.2", "Land, Improvements, Leases (with security deposits), Service Contracts (to the extent assumed), Intangible Property, appurtenant rights (easements, development, air and mineral rights), and tangible personal property owned by Seller and located on or used exclusively at the Property."],
 ["Land", "§1.1 “Land”; Ex. A", "About 22.8 acres (22.800 ± 0.02 ac.) in Fairfax County, VA. Tax Map Parcels 0264-01-0017A, -0017B and -0017C. Shown on “Plat of Resubdivision of Lots 17A, 17B, and 17C, Meridian Corporate Center” (Bowman Consulting, April 22, 2011), Deed Book 24837, Page 1412. Vesting deed: Deed Book 25104, Page 0887. Bounded by Corporate Park Drive, Technology Boulevard, Sunrise Valley Drive and Tax Map Parcel 0264-01-0018. Exhibit A describes the Land as lying in the “Dranesville District.” → Flag 25"],
 ["Improvements", "§1.1 “Improvements”; §7.1(t)", "Three Class A office buildings constructed in 2013: Building A, 11600 Corporate Park Dr. (about 118,000 RSF); Building B, 11620 (about 104,000 RSF); Building C, 11640 (about 90,000 RSF). Total about 312,000 RSF. Structured garage with 1,248 spaces (4.0/1,000 RSF)."],
 ["Occupancy", "Recitals; §3.1; §7.1(g); Ex. F", "14 tenants; 258,140 RSF leased (82.7%; the PSA states “approximately 82%”). By building: A 95.7%, B 81.3%, C 67.4%. Vacant: about 53,860 RSF, of which 29,300 RSF is in Building C."],
 ["Intangible Property", "§1.1; §2.2(f)", "Warranties, guaranties, permits, licenses, approvals, entitlements, development rights, the trade name “Meridian Corporate Center,” domain names, telephone numbers and marketing materials."],
 ["Access / Utilities", "§7.1(p)–(q)", "Legal and physical access to Corporate Park Drive and Technology Boulevard. Public utilities are provided through public rights-of-way or valid easements. Water from Fairfax Water and sewer from Fairfax County (Phase I §2)."],
 ["Permitted Exceptions (pre-agreed)", "§1.1; Ex. B", "(1) Taxes not yet due and payable; (2) Fairfax County zoning, including Planned Development District PD-TC-3; (3) CC&Rs, DB 19842/0387 (office, retail and service uses only; architectural review); (4) Dominion Energy utility easement, DB 20156/1229; (5) County sanitary sewer easement, DB 20156/1245; (6) County stormwater management easement with maintenance obligations, DB 21003/0892; (7) Declaration of Cross-Access Easement and Shared Parking Agreement among the three parcels, DB 23456/0234; (8) Proffers under RZ-2010-PR-024, DB 22789/0567; (9) rights of tenants in possession, as tenants only; (10) ALTA 2021 standard printed exceptions (survey matters, inchoate mechanics’ liens, parties in possession). → Flag 17"],
])

H("3. Purchase Price, Deposits and Closing Funds", 2)
TERMS([
 ["Purchase Price", "§1.1; §3.1", "$87,750,000.00 (about $281.25/RSF; about 10.1x in-place annual base rent of $8,707,892)."],
 ["Initial Deposit", "§1.1; §3.2", "$2,000,000.00 by wire, due within 3 business days after the Effective Date (**October 10, 2024**). Held in a federally insured, interest-bearing account at an institution reasonably acceptable to both parties. Interest follows the Deposit. Buyer’s TIN is used for reporting."],
 ["Additional Deposit", "§1.1; §3.3", "$1,500,000.00 by wire, due within 5 business days after DD expiration (**on or before November 29, 2024**, Thanksgiving excluded). Held on the same terms as the Initial Deposit."],
 ["Total Deposit", "§1.1; §3.3", "$3,500,000.00 (3.99% of the Purchase Price) plus interest. Credited against the Purchase Price at Closing (§3.4)."],
 ["Refundability", "§§4.1, 4.4, 5.3, 7.2, 9.3, 10.2(b), 11.1, 11.2, 12.2", "**Initial Deposit only** is refunded on: DD termination (§4.1/4.4) and financing termination (§10.2(b)). **Full Deposit** is refunded on: uncured title objection (§5.3), material adverse change in a Seller rep (§7.2), estoppel failure (§9.3), Material Casualty (§11.1(a)), Material Condemnation (§11.2(a)) and Seller default (§12.2(b)). Refunds are generally due within 5 business days. → Flag 6"],
 ["Buyer credits at Closing", "§3.5; §6.2; §6.3; §6.4", "Security deposits $487,320.00 plus outstanding TI/LC $1,235,000.00 = **$1,722,320.00** (exclusive of prorations)."],
 ["Indicative cash due at Closing", "§3.5 (computed)", "$87,750,000 − $3,500,000 Deposit − $1,722,320 credits = **$82,527,680** before prorations, closing costs and loan proceeds. With a $57,037,500 loan, the indicative equity due at Closing is about $25,490,180, plus Buyer’s closing costs and plus or minus prorations. Total equity is about $30.71M including the Deposit."],
 ["Wire of net proceeds", "§3.5", "To a Seller-designated account. Seller’s written designation is due at least 3 business days before Closing. → Flag 27 (verify by phone)"],
])

H("4. Due Diligence", 2)
TERMS([
 ["Due Diligence Period", "§1.1; §4.1", "From the Effective Date to **5:00 p.m. ET, November 21, 2024** (45 days). Buyer may investigate in its sole and absolute discretion (environmental, physical, financial, market, zoning, tenant credit) and may terminate for any reason or no reason by written notice before expiration. The Initial Deposit is returned within 5 business days. Failure to give notice is a waiver."],
 ["Termination mechanics", "§4.4; §10.1", "Notice must be delivered by 5:00 p.m. ET on Nov. 21, 2024. Escrow Agent returns the Initial Deposit within 5 business days after receiving notice. No Additional Deposit is owed if it has not yet been posted. If no notice is given, Buyer must post the Additional Deposit."],
 ["Seller deliveries", "§4.2", "Within 5 business days after the Effective Date (about Oct. 14–15, 2024), to the extent in Seller’s possession or reasonable control: Leases with amendments and guaranties; Rent Roll; Service Contracts; environmental reports, surveys and engineering reports (including the Clearfield Phase I dated Aug. 15, 2024); tax bills; operating statements for 2021–2023 and 2024 YTD; certificates of occupancy; insurance policies; plans and as-builts; permits; existing title policies; existing surveys; 24 months of tenant correspondence; roof, elevator and HVAC warranties; and the Metro Parking Solutions garage management agreement. There is no tolling of the DD Period for late delivery. → Flag 24"],
 ["Access", "§4.3", "Reasonable access Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m. ET, on at least 24 hours’ written notice, through Closing. Non-invasive inspections, Phase I/II ESAs, engineering and tenant interviews are permitted. Tenant interviews require Seller’s prior written consent (not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed). Before entry, Buyer must provide evidence of CGL insurance of at least $2,000,000 per occurrence naming Seller as additional insured. → Flag 5"],
 ["Buyer access indemnity", "§4.3", "Buyer indemnifies Seller for loss arising from entry and inspection. Excluded: Seller negligence or willful misconduct and the “discovery of pre-existing conditions.” The indemnity survives termination and is carved out of the liquidated damages limit (§12.1)."],
 ["Due diligence acknowledgment", "§8.2", "Proceeding past the DD Period is deemed an acknowledgment that diligence is complete and satisfactory, and that Buyer relies solely on its own investigations and on the Article VII representations."],
])

 ["Loan", "§10.2(a)", "First mortgage loan from Pinnacle National Bank (or an affiliate) of up to **$57,037,500** (about 65% LTV)."],
 ["Efforts standard", "§10.2(a)", "Buyer must use commercially reasonable and diligent efforts to obtain a commitment on terms satisfactory to Buyer in its reasonable discretion by the **Financing Contingency Deadline, December 6, 2024** (60 days)."],
 ["Termination", "§10.2(b)", "If Buyer cannot obtain a satisfactory commitment despite those efforts, it may terminate by written notice by **5:00 p.m. ET on Dec. 6, 2024**. Escrow Agent returns the **Initial Deposit** within 5 business days. **The PSA does not provide for return of the $1,500,000 Additional Deposit.** → Flag 6"],
 ["Deemed waiver", "§10.2(c)", "Missing the notice means the contingency is irrevocably waived. Buyer must then close whether or not it has financing, and failure to close puts the full $3.5M Deposit at risk as liquidated damages (§12.1)."],
 ["Commitment copy", "§10.2(d)", "Buyer must promptly give Seller a copy of any commitment obtained before the deadline."],
 ["Closing condition", "§9.1(h)", "The Financing Contingency must be satisfied or waived under §10.2. It is effectively a pre-Closing termination right only and is not a condition that survives to Closing."],
])

H("6. Title and Survey", 2)
TERMS([
 ["Title commitment", "§5.1(a)", "Buyer obtains, at its cost, an owner’s title commitment from Commonwealth Title & Escrow LLC with copies of exception documents."],
 ["Survey", "§5.1(b)", "Buyer obtains, at its cost, an ALTA/NSPS survey by a Virginia-licensed surveyor, certified to Buyer, Buyer’s lender and the Title Company. Seller has delivered the existing Bowman Consulting Group survey dated **June 12, 2013**."],
 ["Title Objection Deadline", "§1.1; §5.2", "**November 14, 2024** (38 days). Matters not objected to are deemed Permitted Exceptions. If no objection notice is given, all matters on the commitment and survey are deemed accepted. → Flag 17"],
 ["Seller cure election", "§5.3", "Seller must respond within 15 business days after receiving the objection notice. Seller has no obligation to cure, except that it **must remove** (a) monetary liens of a definite or ascertainable amount (mortgages, deeds of trust, judgments, mechanics’ liens) and (b) encumbrances Seller creates after the Effective Date in violation of the PSA."],
 ["Buyer election", "§5.3", "Within 10 business days after Seller’s notice, Buyer may (i) waive (the matter becomes a Permitted Exception) or (ii) terminate, with the **full Deposit** returned within 5 business days."],
 ["Owner’s policy", "§5.4", "ALTA Owner’s Policy (2021) in the full amount of the Purchase Price ($87,750,000), insuring Buyer or its assignee, subject only to Permitted Exceptions. Buyer pays the premium and all endorsements, including lender endorsements."],
 ["Deed", "§13.2(a); Ex. C", "Special warranty deed (Virginia form) to Bridgewater Capital Partners LLC (or its assignee per §13.2(a)), stating consideration of $87,750,000 and subject to Ex. B Permitted Exceptions. Seller warrants title only against claims by, through or under Seller."],
])
EOF
echo ok'

input.command:
S=/home/user/Lawless_Research_Lab/harvey_lab/sbx.sh; R=/home/user/Lawless_Research_Lab/harvey_lab/vendor/harvey-labs/results/real-estate/extract-psa-key-terms/scenario-01/claude-code-session/20261016-030527; $S $R 'cat > /workspace/build/p3.py <<"EOF"
from h import *
H("7. Seller Representations and Warranties", 2)
P("The representations are made as of the Effective Date and remade at Closing, subject to updating under §7.2 (§7.1).")
TERMS([
 ["(a) Organization/authority", "§7.1(a)", "Virginia LP in good standing, formed Sept. 22, 2011. Meridian GP Inc. is sole GP. Ellison is authorized. No other approvals are required."],

Provide that the cure periods do not extend the Closing Date and that a failure to close on the Closing Date is not subject to cure.")

F(14, "Medium", "No Deposit refund when a closing condition fails without Seller default",
 "§9.1(c), (d), (f), (i); §3.4",
 "Several Buyer conditions have no stated consequence if they fail other than through a Seller default: §9.1(c) (title policy), §9.1(d) (MAC in physical condition, such as a vapor-intrusion finding or structural issue) and §9.1(i) (Seller deliverables). §3.4 returns the Deposit only “as provided in the applicable termination provision.” Buyer could be left unable to close yet without a clear right to recover the Deposit.",
 "Add a general clause: if any §9.1 condition is not satisfied by the Closing Date (as extended), Buyer may terminate and receive the full Deposit, plus expense reimbursement if the failure results from Seller’s breach.")

F(15, "High", "The specific performance deadline conflicts with mandatory mediation and arbitration",
 "§12.2(a); §12.3; §15.4(a)–(b)",
 "§12.2(a) requires Buyer to “commence” a specific performance action within 60 days after the scheduled Closing Date, failing which Buyer is deemed to have elected termination. But §15.4 requires mediation first (commencing within 30 days of demand and running up to 60 days) and then AAA arbitration. Mediation alone could consume the full 60 days, and it is unclear whether “commence” means a mediation demand, an arbitration demand, or a court action. Arbitration also complicates recording a lis pendens to protect Buyer’s position against a sale to a third party. §12.3 contemplates court interpleader in Fairfax County, which is inconsistent with mandatory arbitration of disputes over the Deposit. “Willful” default (§12.2(b)) is undefined.",
 "Provide that a mediation demand or arbitration demand within 60 days satisfies §12.2(a) (or extend it to 90 days and toll it during mediation). Carve specific performance, injunctive relief, lis pendens filings and escrow interpleader out of mediation and arbitration, or expressly permit court actions for them. Define willful default to include Seller’s failure to deliver the deed or deliverables, or a sale or financing to a third party.")

F(16, "Medium", "Rep bring-down timing and the effect of updates",
 "§7.1 (lead-in); §7.2; §9.1(a)",
 "Seller may “update” its reps, and the Seller’s Closing Certificate is delivered **at Closing**. Yet Buyer has 5 business days after receiving it to decide whether to terminate, which cannot work at a simultaneous closing. The PSA does not say whether an update that is not a “material adverse change” (an undefined term) cures the breach for indemnity purposes, or whether Buyer’s closing over a disclosed change waives the claim.",
 "Require delivery of a draft Closing Certificate at least 5 business days before Closing. Provide that updates do not cure breaches or limit indemnity unless caused by events outside Seller’s control occurring after the Effective Date. Define “material adverse change,” for example by dollar thresholds or any change affecting a major tenant.")

F(17, "Medium", "Title and survey mechanics",
 "§1.1 (“Permitted Exceptions”); §5.2; §5.3; Ex. B; §9.1(c)",
 "(i) Exhibit B pre-approves 10 Permitted Exceptions before Buyer has seen the commitment. That includes item 10 (standard survey and mechanics’-lien exceptions), which Pinnacle will require be deleted and which conflicts with Seller’s §5.3(a) obligation to remove mechanics’ liens. Unobjected matters are also “deemed” Permitted Exceptions (§5.2), which conflicts with the §1.1 definition limited to Ex. B. (ii) There is no right to object to **new matters** first disclosed by commitment updates or the survey after Nov. 14 (a gap). (iii) Seller’s silence during the 15-business-day cure period is not addressed. (iv) The Title Objection Deadline (Nov. 14) leaves only 7 days before DD expiry, and the survey may not be complete. (v) The Ex. B Declaration of Cross-Access Easement and Shared Parking Agreement (DB 23456/0234) and the CC&Rs (DB 19842/0387) impose cost-sharing and use limits that need review. If all three parcels are acquired, confirm there is no merger issue for lender insurability. (vi) The proffers (RZ-2010-PR-024) may impose unfulfilled transportation or open-space obligations.",
 "Order the commitment and ALTA/NSPS survey (with Table A items required by Pinnacle) now, so objections can be finalized by Nov. 14. Seek: deletion of Ex. B item 10 for Seller-provided owner’s and gap affidavits; a gap and new-matters objection right through Closing; deemed Seller refusal to cure on silence; and Seller’s obligation to cure Seller-created matters. Obtain a zoning report confirming PD-TC-3 compliance and proffer status.")

F(18, "Medium", "Non-terminable Service Contracts and designation of Assumed Contracts",
 "§1.1 (“Property”); §2.2(e); §7.1(h); §13.2(d); Ex. G; Ex. H ¶3",
 "Three contracts are non-terminable on a change of ownership: Apex Elevator ($148,800/yr through 6/30/2026), Sentinel Fire ($38,400/yr through 12/31/2025) and Metro Parking ($222,000/yr through 3/31/2027). Together they represent about $744,050 of committed spend after a Jan. 15, 2025 Closing. In practice Buyer must assume them, yet the PSA lets Buyer designate Assumed Contracts and Ex. H says Seller remains liable for non-assumed contracts. This conflicts with their non-terminability, and Seller may argue Buyer must take them. No deadline is set for Buyer’s designation, other than “during the Due Diligence Period” in the Ex. H Schedule 1 note. The Metro Parking agreement controls the 1,248-space garage. Its assignment and consent terms, and any revenue-sharing, have not been reviewed.",
 "Review all 11 contracts in the data room, focusing on the Apex, Sentinel and Metro assignment clauses. Designate Assumed Contracts by DD expiry. Require Seller to terminate all non-assumed terminable contracts at its cost effective at Closing. Price the non-terminable contracts into the underwriting, or require Seller to obtain counterparty consent to termination or assignment.")

F(19, "Medium", "Prorations, TI/LC, free rent and reconciliation gaps",
 "§6.1(a), (c); §6.3; §6.4; Ex. F",
 "(i) **Garrison & Holt** (C-500): lease start 9/1/2023 but estimated rent commencement **1/1/2025**. Its $8,910/mo ($106,920/yr) is included in rent roll totals, but if rent commencement slips past Closing, the free-rent burden falls on Buyer. The PSA has no credit for free rent or abatements remaining after Closing. (ii) The TI/LC figure is “approximately” $1,235,000. The credit should be the **actual** unpaid amount, confirmed by estoppels, with Seller paying any excess. §6.3 also describes these as three “pending lease transactions,” though they relate to leases signed in 2022–2023 (CrestLine 8/1/2022; Clearview 5/1/2023; Garrison & Holt 9/1/2023), so the description should be clarified. (iii) The 90-day reconciliation window (through Apr. 15, 2025) is too short for the CY2024 CAM, tax and insurance reconciliations, which typically take place in spring or summer 2025. (iv) It is not stated whether Seller may sue tenants after Closing for delinquent rent. (v) Treatment of tax-appeal refunds is not addressed.",
 "Add a Buyer credit for all free rent, abatements and unfunded landlord work for periods after Closing. Make the TI/LC credit the actual amount (as confirmed by estoppels) with a true-up. Extend the CY2024 reconciliation through Sept. 30, 2025. Bar Seller from suing tenants in possession post-Closing. Allocate tax refunds by period.")

F(20, "Medium", "Litigation disclosure is internally inconsistent",
 "§7.1(e); Sch. 7.1(e); §7.1(i); §7.4(a)",
 "Doe v. Meridian claims about **$175,000**, but the policy deductible is only **$25,000**. §7.1(e) says resolution is expected “below the policy deductible,” while the Schedule says “well within the policy deductible of $25,000.” A $175,000 claim is not “within” a $25,000 deductible. The statements are inconsistent and minimize exposure. The claimed amount also equals the $175,000 rep Basket. The CGL carrier, Pinnacle Casualty Insurance Co., shares a name with the lender (Pinnacle National Bank). That is probably coincidental, but worth confirming.",
 "Confirm that the Doe claim and any other pre-Closing tort claims are an **Excluded Liability**, with Seller indemnification outside the Basket and Cap. Request the complaint, the insurer’s coverage position and the reserve. Correct the rep language in the amendment.")

F(21, "Medium", "Possible tenant purchase rights",
 "§7.1(r); Ex. B item 9; Ex. E ¶8",
 "The no-options rep and Ex. B both carve out purchase rights “expressly set forth in the Leases.” Any ROFR or ROFO (for example, Valerian’s) would be a Permitted Exception and could block or delay the sale.",
 "Confirm through lease review that no tenant holds a ROFR, ROFO or option. If any exists, require a written waiver before DD expiry, and delete the carve-out or make it limited to Leases listed on a schedule.")

F(22, "Medium", "“Business day” is undefined, and several deadlines fall on holidays",
 "§§3.2, 3.3, 4.2, 4.4, 5.3, 9.3, 12.1, 12.2, 13.5, 14.3",
 "Many deadlines run in business days, but the term is undefined. §3.3 excludes Thanksgiving, but other holidays are not addressed: Columbus Day (Oct. 14, 2024) for the §4.2 deliveries, Veterans Day (Nov. 11), Christmas Eve and Day, and New Year’s Day for the estoppel and assignment deadlines. Mar. 1, 2025 (final outside date) is a Saturday, and Mar. 16, 2025 (specific performance deadline) is a Sunday.",
 "Define business day (excluding weekends, federal holidays and days on which banks in Fairfax County, VA are closed), with a roll-forward to the next business day for deadlines.")

F(23, "Medium", "No property management agreement is listed, despite references to an on-site property manager",
 "§7.1(h); §7.1(s); §7.1 (knowledge definition); Ex. G; Phase I §1, §5",
 "§7.1(h) says Ex. G lists all “management” contracts, and §7.1(s) says all on-site management is provided by contractors under Ex. G. Yet Ex. G lists no property management agreement, and the PSA knowledge definition refers to Seller’s “on-site property manager.” The Phase I also interviewed the “on-site property management team retained by the Seller.” Either a management contract is missing from the schedule (a rep inaccuracy) or management is performed by an affiliate under an undocumented arrangement.",
 "Require Seller to identify the property manager and the agreement, terminate it at Seller’s cost effective at Closing, and correct Ex. G. Confirm there are no employees or union obligations transferring to Buyer.")

F(24, "Medium", "Diligence deliveries and reliance on Seller materials",
 "§4.2; §8.1(VI); §8.2",
 "Deliveries were due on about Oct. 14–15, 2024, with no tolling of the DD Period if they are late, and only “to the extent in Seller’s possession or reasonable control.” §8.1(VI) disclaims the accuracy of all delivered information, including operating statements that Pinnacle and the IC will underwrite. §4.2(d) lists the Clearfield Phase I as a Seller deliverable, even though Calverley commissioned it.",
 "Confirm today what is in the data room and send a deficiency list. Request a day-for-day DD extension for late deliveries. Ask for a limited rep that the operating statements were prepared in the ordinary course and are true and correct in all material respects. Confirm whether Seller has any other environmental reports.")

F(25, "Medium", "Legal description and survey points to verify",
 "Ex. A; §5.1(b); Phase I §§2–3",
 "(i) Ex. A places the Land in the “Dranesville District” of Fairfax County. Reston is generally within the Hunter Mill Supervisor District, so the reference should be checked against the vesting deed and plat. (ii) Ex. A identifies Tax Map Parcel 0264-01-0018 along the southern boundary, while the Phase I places the former dry-cleaner parcel (0264-01-0019) immediately to the southwest. The survey should confirm whether 0019 actually adjoins the Property and where the Building C boundary sits relative to it. That matters for the Phase II well locations and for any contiguous-property-owner analysis. (iii) The only existing survey is from June 12, 2013, and the plat dates from April 22, 2011, before Seller’s formation on Sept. 22, 2011. Confirm the chain of title through DB 25104/0887.",
 "Instruct the surveyor to plot all Ex. B easements, confirm the legal description closes and matches 22.800 acres, show adjoining parcels by tax map number (including 0264-01-0019), and locate the stormwater ponds and easements. Have the title company confirm the supervisor district reference and the vesting chain.")

F(26, "Medium", "Casualty provisions favor Seller",
 "§1.1 (“Material Casualty”); §11.1",
 "(i) Below $4,000,000, Buyer must close with only an assignment of insurance proceeds plus the deductible. There is no protection if a casualty is uninsured or underinsured, if rent-loss proceeds are not assigned, or if a major tenant gains a casualty termination right. (ii) Materiality is measured against Seller’s own “good faith estimate.” (iii) Buyer’s silence for 15 days is deemed an election to close. (iv) Notice does not extend Closing to allow the 15-day election.",
 "Add: Buyer termination right if any tenant over 15,000 RSF may terminate, or if the casualty is uninsured; a credit for uninsured amounts; assignment of rent-loss proceeds for post-Closing periods; materiality determined by an independent adjuster or architect; deemed election to **terminate** on silence (or at least a Closing extension to allow the election).")

F(27, "High", "Notice e-mail addresses are inconsistent, creating defective-notice and wire-fraud risk",
 "§15.2; §3.5; §1.1 (Escrow Agent)",
 "The notice block shows Buyer counsel as jhargrave@**hmstone.com**, while HMS uses @**hmslegal.com**. Seller’s counsel, Ferndale & Aldrich LLP, is shown as saldrich@**fenwickaldrich.com**. Buyer’s GC uses @bridgewatercap.com for a Calverley notice address. E-mail notice is effective only if followed by overnight courier within 1 business day. With time-critical termination notices (DD on Nov. 21, financing on Dec. 6), a misdirected or disputed notice could be fatal. Mismatched domains are also a classic sign of business-e-mail-compromise wire fraud, which matters for the deposit wires and the Seller payoff wire (§3.5).",
 "Correct all notice addresses by amendment. Deliver all termination and election notices by hand or overnight courier **and** e-mail, timed to arrive well before 5:00 p.m. ET on the deadline. Verify all wiring instructions (Initial Deposit, Additional Deposit, closing funds) by telephone call-back to a known number (Jennifer Walsh, Commonwealth Title). Do not rely on e-mailed instructions.")

F(28, "Medium", "Recordation tax and closing cost allocation",
 "§13.4(a)–(c)",
 "“All recording fees and charges” likely places the Virginia grantee recordation taxes on Buyer. By our estimate, that is about $219,375 state plus about $73,125 local on the deed (at $0.25 per $100 and one-third of state), plus about $190,125 on a $57.04M deed of trust. These are estimates to be confirmed with Commonwealth Title. Seller pays the grantor’s tax. The Northern Virginia regional congestion relief fee on grantors is not expressly allocated, so it falls to Fairfax custom under §13.4(c).",
 "Confirm the closing-cost budget with Commonwealth Title. Expressly allocate the grantor’s tax and the regional congestion relief fee to Seller. Explore deed-of-trust tax structuring with Pinnacle.")

F(29, "Medium (business)", "Leasing rollover and concentration risk",
 "Ex. F; §7.1(g)",
 "About 60% of leased RSF (155,240 RSF) expires by 12/31/2027. RedPoint (22,500 RSF) expires 8/31/2025 and holds a 90-day early-termination right (as early as about April 2025). Chesapeake (31,200 RSF; 12/31/2026) has no renewal option. Valerian is 24.2% of RSF and about 25.8% of rent (expires 3/31/2029). Building C is only 67.4% leased and sits in the REC area. These matters are not PSA defects, but they bear on price, lender DSCR and reserve sizing.",
 "Conduct tenant interviews (with §4.3 consent) and credit reviews for Valerian, NovaTech, Chesapeake, Athena and RedPoint. Request any RedPoint termination notice status in the estoppel. Consider a rollover reserve or price adjustment. Confirm Valerian’s government-contract funding and any security-clearance or SCIF requirements affecting the assignment of the lease.")

F(30, "Medium", "Phase I is an executive summary only, with internal inconsistencies",
 "Phase I preamble, §§2–3, 7, 8",
 "We reviewed only the Executive Summary, which states it should not be relied on alone. Items to reconcile: §2 says there was no development before 2011 and construction commenced in 2012, while §3 says the **2010** aerial shows active grading “consistent with the commencement of construction activities in 2012.” Clearfield’s liability is limited to its fee (§8, item 5). Clearfield recommends a DEQ FOIA request for the complete VRP-00487 file, including any institutional controls.",
 "Obtain the full Phase I report and appendices (especially Appendix F, the DEQ VRP records). Ask Clearfield to reconcile the site-history dates. Negotiate a higher liability limit for the Phase II. Submit the FOIA request now.")
EOF
echo ok'

The Seller indemnity in §8.4 is capped at **\$3,000,000** (3.4% of price), lasts only **36 months** (to January 15, 2028), and is given by a single-asset seller with no credit support. In addition, the Seller environmental representation in §7.1(k) excludes everything disclosed in the Phase I (Flags 2--4).
31:- **3. The Phase II cannot be finished inside the Due Diligence Period (Critical).** Clearfield needs 10--14 business days to mobilize and then 4--6 weeks after field work to produce results. Even if work is authorized now, results are unlikely before early-to-mid December 2024, which is after the November 21 expiration (Flag 5).
